name: scatter_santali
description: Santali — the most widely spoken language of the Munda people (Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, Assam; written in its own Ol Chiki script as well as Devanagari, Bengali, and Roman); sister languages include Mundari, Korku, Ho, Sora — on the standardized 12-column place axis. Santali's deep contact with Sanskritic / Indic languages has integrated a full 4-way stop voicing/aspiration contrast (voiceless, voiceless-aspirated, voiced, voiced-aspirated) across 5 places — the same matrix structure as Sanskrit, but built from Indic absorption rather than native engineering. Four matched nasals (m, n, ɲ, ŋ). The retroflex flap /ɽ/ joins the alveolar lateral /l/ in the liquids row. Sibilant /s/, glottal /h/, trill /r/, glides /w, j/. 31 cells filled — the densest of the three Munda charts shown, and the visible record of Indic absorption into the lineage.
